zh.principle:
**算法**：Rabin 陷门公钥密码（Rabin Cryptosystem）。### 二次剩余陷门

Rabin 签名把消息哈希映射到模 n 的二次剩余，签名是方程 x²+bx≡H(m,u) 的一个根。公钥是 n=pq 与常数 b；私钥 p,q 用于在 Z_p、Z_q 上开方，再用 CRT 合并。### 四根与编码

平方映射的每个值有四个根；签名者只公开一个，两个不同根会泄露 gcd 从而分解 n。标准化变体用 Rabin-Williams 编码和冗余，并把随机串 u 纳入哈希，避免根选择歧义和选择消息攻击。### 安全归约

在随机预言机模型下，伪造签名可归约为求模 n 平方根，而求平方根与分解 n 等价。验证只需一次模平方和编码检查，比 RSA 的模幂快数百倍。
zh.why: Rabin 是第一个可证明“伪造难度等价于分解大整数”的实用签名族。RSA 只做到“破签不比分解更难”，Rabin 给出反向归约：能从伪造推出因子。验签一次平方，签名端一次开方加 CRT，计算量都低于同规模 RSA；这让它适合智能卡、传感器和低功耗验证方。代价是签名端要处理四根与编码，工程上比 RSA 难用，标准化版本转向 Rabin-Williams。
zh.used: Rabin-Williams 变体进入 ISO/IEC 14888-2（带附录签名）与 ISO/IEC 9796-2（消息恢复签名），IEEE P1363 也收录 Rabin；主要用于标准教材、嵌入式验签和需要可证明因子分解安全的场景。实际部署远少于 RSA：签名是概率性的，根选择、编码和专利/生态都增加成本；现代 TLS、代码签名和证书几乎只用 RSA、ECDSA 或 Ed25519。
zh.broken: 裸平方根签名对选择消息攻击脆弱：攻击者取随机 x，请求签 x² mod n；若返回的根不是 ±x，gcd(x−s,n) 直接给出 p 或 q。必须用带冗余的编码和随机化哈希阻断。ISO 9796-2 的 Rabin-Williams 实例曾被 Coron–Naccache–Stern 类攻击和后续改进攻击；哈希太短或编码不当会允许伪造。参数、编码和根的选择都必须按标准执行。
zh.history:
Rabin 1979 年在 MIT/LCS/TR-212 提出该方案；Williams 1980 给出 Rabin-Williams 变体，使签名更接近 RSA 形式；Bellare–Rogaway 1996 给出精确安全界；随后进入 ISO/IEC 14888-2 与 9796-2。它影响了可证明安全签名和基于分解的密码学，但因工程复杂性未成为主流。

en.principle:
**Algorithm**: Rabin Cryptosystem (Rabin 陷门公钥密码). ### Quadratic-residue trapdoor

A Rabin signature hashes the message to a quadratic residue modulo n and returns a root of x²+bx≡H(m,u). The public key is n=pq and a constant b; the private factors p,q let the signer take square roots modulo each prime and combine them with CRT. ### Four roots and encoding

Squaring has four roots for every value. The signer publishes only one; two distinct roots leak gcd and factor n. Standardized Rabin-Williams variants add redundancy, encode the message, and bind a random string u into the hash to prevent root ambiguity and chosen-message attacks. ### Security reduction

In the random oracle model, forging reduces to computing a square root modulo n, which is equivalent to factoring n. Verification is one modular squaring plus an encoding check, hundreds of times faster than an RSA modular exponentiation.
en.why:
Rabin was the first practical signature family proven “forging is as hard as factoring”. RSA only gives “breaking signatures is no harder than factoring”; Rabin gives the converse reduction from forgery to factors.

Verification is one squaring, and signing is one square-root extraction plus CRT, both cheaper than RSA at the same modulus size. That suits smart cards, sensors and low-power verifiers. The price is four-root handling and encoding, which made it harder to engineer than RSA; standardized variants moved to Rabin-Williams.
en.used:
Rabin-Williams variants appear in ISO/IEC 14888-2 (signatures with appendix) and ISO/IEC 9796-2 (message-recovery signatures), and IEEE P1363 includes Rabin. Uses are mainly standards education, embedded verification and settings that want a factoring-equivalence proof.

Real deployment is far below RSA: signatures are probabilistic, root selection and encoding add cost, and patent/ecosystem effects favor RSA, ECDSA or Ed25519 in modern TLS, code signing and certificates.

en.broken:
A raw square-root signature is vulnerable to a chosen-message attack: the attacker picks random x and asks for a signature on x² mod n. If the returned root is not ±x, gcd(x−s,n) directly reveals p or q. Redundant encoding and randomized hashing are required.

The Rabin-Williams instance in ISO 9796-2 was hit by Coron–Naccache–Stern-style attacks and later improvements; short hashes or careless encoding enable forgery. Parameters, encoding and root selection must follow the standard.
en.history:
Rabin proposed the scheme in MIT/LCS/TR-212 in 1979; Williams gave the Rabin-Williams variant in 1980, making signatures closer to RSA form; Bellare and Rogaway gave exact security bounds in 1996; it later entered ISO/IEC 14888-2 and 9796-2.

It influenced provably secure signatures and factorization-based cryptography, but engineering complexity kept it out of the mainstream.
